content.text:
I fixed it with a one-line change in `lib/adapters/http.js:474`. I haven't run any tests or tried it against a real response.

The http adapter picks how to decompress by looking at the `content-encoding` header, and it compared the raw value to lowercase names like `'gzip'`. A response with `GZIP` (such as the ones from storage.googleapis.com) or `Gzip` matched nothing, so the body was never decompressed. The adapter now converts the value to lowercase before that comparison, so any capitalisation of `gzip`, `x-gzip`, `compress`, `x-compress`, `deflate` or `br` is decompressed.

The new line is `(res.headers['content-encoding'] || '').toLowerCase()`. The `|| ''` is there because HEAD and 204 responses delete the header just before this point, and calling `.toLowerCase()` on the missing value would throw.
